description: A duo of talented students from TUM. We are specialists on scientifical research as well as on marketing and customer analysis. Together, we plan to deliver software that is useful and attractive at both the theoretical and practical levels.
summary:
We developed an interactive web visualizer built using JavaScript,
HTML, and CSS for the frontend and Python for the backend. The application
executes live queries against NASA’s SPHEREx sky-cutout datasets while
cross-matching and retrieving quality-flag metadata from both the Gaia and
WISE catalogs. The platform provides accesible but useful spectrophotometric
analysis tools to inspect observations across specific wavelength
bands, alongside multi-epoch image processing features such as frame
mean (co-addition) and difference imaging within the same spectral
bandpass. The tool also integrates Aladin Lite to
astrometrically cross-verify cutouts against target Right Ascension
(RA) and Declination (Dec) coordinates, featuring adjustable Field of
View (FoV) controls and multiple time-frame visualization modes (raw,
smoothed, and RGB).
details:
• Opening the page calls GET /api/state to load release metadata, presets, and the initial sky view, and triggers POST /api/batch to load the remaining preset targets in the background.
  • Requesting a sky position calls GET /api/sky. The backend queries IRSA's SIA v2 endpoint to find matching SPHEREx exposures inside the requested release and time window (0.5–15 years), while running concurrent cone searches on IRSA Gator for Gaia DR3 and AllWISE catalog sources.
  • For selected exposures covering the field center, the server downloads compact FITS cutouts from IRSA IBE, masks fatal bitmask flags, reads local wavelengths and bandwidths from the FITS spectral WCS, and reprojects each frame onto a shared north-up, east-left 64×64 pixel grid encoded as Base64 typed arrays.
  • app.js Decodes the sky cube once in memory so switching modes (Blink, Mean (+), Diff (-)), detectors (D1–D6, Available arrays, Spatial smoothing, RGB), Spectral FFT filters, FOV sizes, catalog overlays, and timeline brushes updates locally; such features are available on-demand thanks to the user interface, which focuses on simplicity and practicality, focusing on fundamental Data Visualization design principles.
